clue.text: In spite of entanglement, spoken of with repute

indicators.note: something spoken is heard rather than read, so the sound of the preceding word is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: a knot is a tangle; said out loud it matches a word of negation
taken as written
one's standing is one's reputation

explanation.surface: Someone is honoured despite having been caught up in a tangle of scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding is a formal preposition meaning despite, used to concede a point before carrying on regardless.

clue.text: Dribbling on one's toes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a footballer dribbling keeps possession at their feet
second meaning: alert and quick to react

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the literal football picture; the second is the everyday idiom for being sharp and attentive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone alert and quick-witted, while a dribbling player literally has possession of the football.

clue.text: Western Aid for 27

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for western
to aid is to help

explanation.surface: A cowboy charity appeal for a young bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answer to 27 Down is CUB, and a WHELP is a young animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a puppy or other young carnivore, so it serves as a synonym for the young animal at 27 Down.

clue.text: To earth's lowest end

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical wiring; that the letters also run on unbroken in the clue is a coincidence, not a hiding device

explanation.surface: Something digs down to the very bottom of the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are the body's extremity furthest down, so the foot's tip is literally its lowest point.

clue.text: Like Weller and Geldof's band, given up fame

indicators.note: in a down clue, something sent up is read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Paul Weller, of the Jam, is nicknamed the Modfather, the icon of the mod youth movement
Bob Geldof fronted the Boomtown Rats

explanation.surface: Two rock stars' bands have given up on celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a British 1960s youth subculture of sharp suits and scooters, revived in the late 70s with Weller as its figurehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being a celebrity, which amounts to great fame or renown.

clue.text: I'm unfit, and I exercised endlessly

indicators.note: exercised suggests being worked hard and moved about, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: An unfit person complains of having worked out without end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means without limit, describing something repeated forever, which matches endlessly as an adverb.

clue.text: Realise how to produce popular TV show?

parts.words: Realise how to produce popular TV show?
parts.note: surface reading: working out the secret of making a hit programme
setter's reading: the answer, taken as an instruction, rearranges a three-letter question word to produce the word how

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the title as an order, 'doctor' (tamper with) the word WHO, and you produce HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC science fiction series about a time-travelling Time Lord is one of Britain's most popular television programmes.

clue.text: Spirit never mixed

indicators.note: something mixed has been stirred together, so the preceding letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cocktail note: this liquor has never been blended.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means courage or boldness, the same sense as spirit when praising someone's mettle.

clue.text: Create revolution, following Egypt and the rest

indicators.note: following tells us these letters come after the country's abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: ET is the international vehicle registration code for Egypt

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters of the preceding word are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to stir up a revolt in Egypt and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, usually shortened to etc, closes a list to mean and other things of the same kind.

clue.text: Becomes liable for fashionable dogs

parts.note: something in is in fashion
curs are mongrel dogs

explanation.surface: Someone owning trendy dogs ends up paying for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it on oneself, becoming responsible for paying it.

clue.text: Folk music genre encapsulating English language's extremes

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so the outer letters wrap around the abbreviation for the nationality

parts.note: pop is a genre of popular music

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of language
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A folk musician's style is said to sum up English at its extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk music' looks like the genre, but folk alone is the definition and music genre gives the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk is an informal word for persons in general, exactly as people is used.

clue.text: Annoyed former lover (according to new date)

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: as per means in accordance with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated with an ex who has rearranged their meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperated describes someone intensely irritated or frustrated, a stronger form of being annoyed.

clue.text: Lie with maid in grass, catching wild animal on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the whole combination is read backwards
catching means holding something inside, so the plant word wraps around the animal word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
the wolf is a wild animal

explanation.surface: A rustic seduction in the long grass, interrupted by a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie with maid in grass' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is only a link and the grass belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflower is an old-fashioned euphemism for taking a woman's virginity, which is what lying with a maiden implies.

clue.text: Meat provides end to rear game

indicators.note: providing the end means these letters are attached as the final part, after the other word

parts.note: the rear is the back
gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: A butcher's tip: meat is the way to finish off raising game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear game' looks like raising animals, but rear gives the first half and game is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by the throw of dice.

clue.text: Thrill starting a fight in casual football game

indicators.note: starting means coming at the beginning, so the excitement word goes in front of the rest

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, as in getting a kick out of something
taken as written
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: The excitement of starting a scrap during an informal game of football.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickabout is an informal game of football with no set teams or rules, played for fun.

clue.text: Heterosexual married couple embracing when clean?

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the pair of letters surrounds the time word

parts.note: a married man and woman are W for wife and H for husband, standard abbreviations
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a married couple's cuddle is wholesome.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash is to clean something with water, making the two verbs direct synonyms.

clue.text: Likeness of alien suppressed by legal order

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down inside something else, so the alien goes within the legal word

parts.note: a statute is a written law
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A picture of an alien banned by court order.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette is a small sculpted figure, a likeness of a person or creature in miniature.

clue.text: Union bar closes early

indicators.note: closing early means stopping before the end, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: to bar is to block

explanation.surface: The student union bar shuts before its usual time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union bar' reads as one place, the students' drinking spot; union is the definition and bar the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries or parties acting together, so it is a union of interests.

clue.text: Platoon is ordered to skirt one concerning location

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edges, so the rearranged letters surround the numeral
ordered means arranged into a fresh sequence, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A platoon is told to march round a single soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Positional means relating to position, and a position is a place or location.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing type of chants and mantras, without beginning or end

indicators.note: dropping both the beginning and the end leaves only the inner part of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the phrase, once its outer parts are dropped

explanation.surface: Endless chants and mantras that send people off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore the Sandman sprinkles sand in children's eyes to make them fall asleep, so he is a figure who induces sleep.

clue.text: He's one of four siblings, possibly reading into child's detachment

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the preceding pieces are placed within the child word

parts.note: a son is a child

parts.words: He's one of four siblings, possibly
parts.note: a quad is a quadruplet, one of four born together
reading is one of the three Rs of basic education

explanation.surface: One of four brothers reads aloud a story into his child's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a military unit, and detachment is a word for a body of troops sent on a separate task.

clue.text: Witticism inscribed on university's old recording equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing something on top of another piece places it first, above the following letter

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A joke engraved on a university's antique tape recorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tape deck, but the answer is an Inca device of knotted strings used to keep records.
explanation.definitionFit: The quipu was a set of knotted cords the Incas used to record numbers and information, so it was ancient record-keeping equipment.

clue.text: Make fun of cheerful dummy

parts.note: to mock is to ridicule
feeling up means in good spirits

explanation.surface: Someone teases a happy fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dummy' looks like an insult for a person; it means a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-up is a full-size model or prototype for testing a design, the sense of dummy as a stand-in replica.

clue.text: Freight from Columbus' first legendary ship

indicators.note: first means the opening position, so only the initial letter of the explorer's name is used

parts.note: the initial letter of Columbus
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend

explanation.surface: Goods unloaded from the explorer's flagship of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbus suggests the Santa Maria, but the legendary ship is the Argo of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship or aircraft, which is exactly what freight means.

clue.text: A number with disease caused by rich food in feast

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the constant is placed next to the illness

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant
gout is a painful joint disease long linked to rich eating and drinking

explanation.surface: Someone at a banquet falls ill from overindulging in rich food.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is a slang phrase for eating greedily, which is how one would feast.

clue.text: Club tariff is steep

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a tariff is a fixed rate of charge

explanation.surface: A nightclub's entry charge is very expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for a high price; it is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften food by soaking it in liquid, which is what steeping does.

clue.text: Country, short in youth

indicators.note: something short is lacking its full length, so the last letter of the country goes

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean country

explanation.surface: A nation that falls short when it comes to its young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is an inexperienced young person, as in cub reporter, so it stands for a youth.

clue.text: Formally attired in all clubs perhaps, then kicked out

parts.note: a card hand all in clubs, or any one suit, is suited
then means and also
to boot out is to kick out

explanation.surface: Nightclub bouncers throw someone out despite their smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs, but it is the card suit, and a hand all in one suit is suited.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone dressed up smartly in a suit and boots, so formally attired for an occasion.
